root_idea.summary: The root centers on whiteness appearing through or mixed with blackness, rather than pure white.
root_idea.development: This contrast develops into terms for gray or hoary color, bright fire and shooting stars, and further Classical applications to altered vegetation, whitened weapons, barren or wintry conditions, and figurative sharpness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular dictionary citation form شِهَاب.
شُهُب is the attested broken plural of شِهَاب and is presented under the singular headword.

senses.definition: A bright flame or firebrand of fire, including a torch or flaming fire.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for a conspicuously blazing flame or a firebrand; the plural form شُهُب is included under this headword.

senses.definition: A shooting or falling star, or a flaming celestial projectile, especially one sent after a devil.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic celestial-fire construction associated with pursuing devils and with an apparition in the sky; both شِهَاب and its plural شُهُب occur in this lexical branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become gray: whiteness predominates over, or is interrupted by, blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A color description formed from mixed whiteness rather than pure white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alter another's color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of heat or cold; cold may alter the color of trees or people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a year of drought to destroy a people's livestock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for the destructive effect of a barren year on property and cattle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a stallion or a man, to have offspring of the gray or mixed-white-and-black color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is explained with differing attributions concerning whether it is said of the stallion or of the owner of the horses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of seedproduce, to dry or become yellow while retaining some green, and to approach yielding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a crop or seedproduce that has dried and lightened but is not entirely devoid of green.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the lips, to become ashy in hue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A color change specifically applied to the lips.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mountain overspread with snow.
A boy or young man who is light or active in body and sharp-headed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A description of bodily agility and quickness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gray or hoary color in which whiteness is mixed with or interrupted by blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In horses, the term covers a coat whose main hue is interrupted by hoariness or white hairs, whether the underlying color is bay, chestnut, or black.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant resembling panic grass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name, also reported in the variant form شَبَهَان.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Milk mixed with much water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may refer to a mixture of about one-third milk and the remainder water; the name is connected with the resulting alteration of color.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shining or brightly shining stars; in one usage, the seven stars or planets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical plural usage distinct from the Quranic shooting-star construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A penetrating, sharp, or energetic person, especially in war; figuratively, a brave or hero of an army.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative comparison with the force or brilliance of a shooting star.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a certain devil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested as a proper name in traditional usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gray or mixed white-and-black in color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a male horse or mule and, in the feminine شَهْبَاء, to a female mule or goat and to a blaze containing hairs of a different color. The plural الأَشَاهِب was also used for a troop associated with comeliness or white faces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light-colored or whitened through the reduction or contrast of blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to ambergris of excellent pale color, to an iron head or blade lightly filed so that some or all of its blackness is removed, and to a troop whose weapons appear bright or white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Barren, sterile, or wintry in a way associated with whiteness or bleakness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to land or a year lacking verdure, to a cold or frost-laden day or night, and to the three bright white nights of the lunar month.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard or difficult, especially an affair or case that is disliked or beyond one's power to accomplish or endure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjective applied to an arduous matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lion.
The hedgehog.
